0.headline: Diaper maker Nobel Hygiene gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
0.heading: Diaper maker Nobel Hygiene gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
0.intro: The issue comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs.150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 15,511,082 equity shares by existing shareholders
0.body:
Nobel Hygiene Limited, India's largest home-grown branded manufacturer of absorbent hygiene products, including diapers, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The issue comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 15,511,082 equity shares by existing shareholders. These include promoters Kamal Kumar Johari and Kamini Kamal Johari, along with investor shareholders Orbit Investment Holdings Pte. Ltd., Sixth Sense India Opportunities III, Bennett Trading LLP, Manish Dharanendra Ladage, Seema Manish Ladage and Lashit Lallubhai Sanghvi.

The net proceeds from the fresh issue are proposed to be used for prepayment or repayment of certain outstanding borrowings; investment in its subsidiary, Nobel Hygiene Baroda Private Limited (NHBPL), to part-finance the expansion of production capacity at Halol; setting up a brownfield manufacturing-cum-warehousing facility on the existing Halol land; and purchasing and installing an adult diaper machine line. A portion of the proceeds will also be used for general corporate purposes.

Nobel Hygiene has a legacy spanning more than two decades and operates across the adult, baby and feminine absorbent hygiene categories through its brands Friends, B-Fit, Teddyy, Snuggy and RIO. Its portfolio comprised more than 1,158 stock-keeping units (SKUs) as of March 31, 2026, covering adult diapers, baby diapers, underpads, insert pads, maternity pads, bed bath towels, wet wipes and sanitary pads. Friends is India's largest adult absorbent hygiene brand by value, while the company has developed a diversified portfolio across multiple price points and usage needs.

The company has established a strong position in the organised absorbent hygiene market. In FY26, adult diapers contributed 49.25% and baby diapers 45.32% of revenue from operations. Friends and Teddyy accounted for 37.85% and 39.63%, respectively, of revenue from operations, while B-Fit contributed 10.83%.

Nobel Hygiene operates 14 manufacturing lines across approximately 19 acres at its Nashik and Halol facilities, with an aggregate annual installed capacity of 1,890.57 million units across adult diapers, baby diapers and underpads.

Its pan-India distribution network spans 0.27 million retail outlets across 31 states and Union Territories, supported by more than 296 stockists and 418 distributors. The company also exports to 19 countries, including Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates, Australia and Mauritius.

On the financial front, revenue from operations increased 14.56% from Rs 739.14 crore in FY25 to Rs 846.75 crore in FY26. EBITDA rose from Rs 65.57 crore to Rs 84.76 crore, while the EBITDA margin improved from 8.87% to 10.01%.

The company also turned profitable, with restated profit for the year rising from Rs 2.28 crore in FY25 to Rs 18.91 crore in FY26. Product margin improved from 42.13% in FY25 to 44.43% in FY26.

Nobel Hygiene also plans to strengthen its presence in the feminine absorbent hygiene category through the introduction of disposable period panties. It will continue to expand its adult and baby hygiene businesses through deeper market penetration, product innovation and increased manufacturing capacity.

ICICI Securities Limited, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Limited and SBI Capital Markets Limited are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

1.headline: Foodlink F&B Holdings IPO subscribed 1.4 times on Day 2 so far; retail portion booked 4 times
1.heading: Foodlink F&B Holdings IPO subscribed 1.4 times on Day 2 so far; retail portion booked 4 times
1.intro: Foodlink is expected to debut on the stock market on December 3.
1.body:
Foodlink F&amp;B Holdings (India) Ltd initial public offering (IPO) continues to see robust demand for the second day of its share sale in the primary market, led by retail investors and QIBs. The Rs 361-crore IPO was fully subscribed on the first day of bidding.

The issue has received bids for 1.44 crore 30 shares as against 1.04 crore shares on offer, as per NSE data, till 2 pm.

The category for retail investors was subscribed 4 times and the portion for Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) also received full subscription at 1.01 times. The quota for non-institutional investors was subscribed 50 per cent.

Earlier, it raised Rs 162.34 crore from anchor investors.
Check All IPO News
The IPO will conclude on November 30, with a price band of Rs 181-191 per share.

The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets.

A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants &amp; Catering Services LLC, to fund the setting up of four new casual dining restaurants.

The funds will also be used for repayment or prepayment of outstanding borrowings and general corporate purposes.

Foodlink F&amp;B Holdings (India) is a luxury food services business focused on providing curated culinary experiences. Its business model comprises event catering, casual dining restaurants, cloud kitchens and banquets and integrated food and beverage services.

The company operates several casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens under brands such as India Bistro, Art of Dum, China Bistro and Glocal in India and the United Arab Emirates.

In its events catering business, the company counts Hardcastle Restaurants, the master franchisee operator of McDonald's in western and southern India, Zee Entertainment and Greenply among its clients.

Foodlink is expected to debut on the stock market on December 3.

2.headline: Swara Baby Products sets Rs 105-111 price band for IPO; plans 10-line capacity expansion
2.heading: Swara Baby Products sets Rs 105-111 price band for IPO; plans 10-line capacity expansion
2.intro: Swara management said it plans to invest Rs.198.2 crore of the fresh issue proceeds in its new manufacturing project at Pithampur in Madhya Pradesh, which will take the production lines at the new project, taking its total to 30 from 20.
2.body:
Swara Baby Products Ltd will open its Rs.800-crore initial public offering on December 2 at a price band of Rs.105-111 per share, as the contract manufacturer seeks fresh capital to expand capacity and repay borrowings. The three-day issue will close on December 4, while anchor investors can bid on December 1.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs.500 crore and an offer for sale of Rs.300 crore. Brainbees Solutions Ltd, which runs FirstCry, and promoter entity Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will each sell shares worth up to Rs.150 crore.

Promoters, who currently own the entire company, will retain a combined 75.09 percent stake after the listing, Chief Business Officer Vaibhav Dangi told Moneycontrol.

Swara management said it plans to invest Rs.198.2 crore of the fresh issue proceeds in its new manufacturing project at Pithampur in Madhya Pradesh, which will take the production lines at the new project, taking its total to 30 from 20.

"The expansion, part of a broader Rs.540-crore capital expenditure programme, is scheduled for completion by the second quarter of FY28 and will increase capacity by about 52 percent," said Alok Birla, chairman and managing director of Swara.

Birla said Swara has already invested over Rs.250 crore in the project through internal accruals and borrowings, with land, buildings and supporting infrastructure largely in place.

Another Rs.100 crore will be used to repay the company’s borrowings and Rs.27.5 crore will be invested in subsidiaries to reduce their debt. The remaining proceeds will support acquisitions, strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes, the management said.

“We have been continuously adding machines,” Dangi said. “In 2024, we were operating 14 lines, in 2025 we operated 17 lines and in 2026 we operated 20 lines.”

Swara started with a single baby-diaper line in 2018. It now manufactures finished products for brands, covering product design, raw-material sourcing, testing, automated manufacturing, packaging and dispatch.

Swara reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs.1,163.9 crore, up 23.4 percent from Rs.942.98 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to Rs.192.77 crore from Rs.162.72 crore, though the EBITDA margin narrowed to 15.9 percent from 16.96 percent.

Baby diapers contributed roughly 70 percent of FY26 revenue, adult incontinence products about 20 percent and feminine hygiene products 10 percent. Swara also sells its Cuddles (baby diaper) and Shields (adult diaper) home brands, which contribute around 18-20 percent of revenue, but management said its growth focus would remain contract manufacturing.

Its customers include Piramal Pharma Ltd, Himalaya Wellness Company and Brainbees Solutions, among 140 customers. The company held 38 percent of India’s baby-diaper contract manufacturing market, 36 percent of adult diapers and 4.3 percent of sanitary napkins by value in FY26.

Growth is being supported by low product penetration, estimated at about 30 percent for baby diapers, 20 percent for sanitary napkins and 5 percent for adult diapers. Accoding to Swara DRHP, India’s diaper and sanitary-napkin manufacturing market is projected to expand to Rs.32,340 crore by 2030 from Rs.17,710 crore in 2025, while contract manufacturing is expected to grow faster as D2C and private-label brands expand.
